analytical_question: Can the organization run a bounded pilot now and what must it demonstrate before operational rollout?
general_et_finding: The selected LLM has unmeasured reliability for this task. Generated claims require evaluation.
application_finding: Conditional fit for evidence-linked drafting with buyer verification and manual sourcing decisions. The assistant remains read-only and cannot select suppliers.
organization_specific_finding: Leadership/sponsorship: Partial: charter and coordinator named | Skills/training: Strength: buyers rehearsed verification and escalation | Workflow/process: Strength: manual approval and rehearsed fallback | Infrastructure/data: Strength: approved read-only environment and verified packet identifiers | Resources/budget: Strength for pilot: funded charter and protected review time. Recurring capacity unknown | Governance/risk: Unknown: delegated stop authority and backup unverified | Culture/change: Partial: rehearsal supports error reporting. Sustained uptake unknown | Operating ownership: Partial: coordinator is named but decision rights unverified. Dominant readiness issue: A coordinator title leaves stop authority and incident coverage unresolved.

evidence.claim: The procurement director signed a pilot charter and named the procurement operations manager as coordinator. Two buyers completed a source-check and escalation rehearsal, and a category manager signs a manual comparison before any sourcing approval. IT/security approved the read-only sandbox and sanitized data boundary. A procurement analyst checked supplier IDs and revision labels for all 20 historical packets against the approved source. The charter funds sandbox usage and protects four reviewer hours per week. The team tested error reporting and manual fallback in a rehearsal. Procurement Operations coordinates the pilot log and weekly review. The case summary does not identify who may pause the pilot or who covers an incident when the coordinator is unavailable. The charter covers four weeks. Recurring staffing and funding after the pilot have not been decided.
evidence.notes: Readiness judgments are inferences from these stipulated capabilities.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Fictional profile. Assessments were produced in one Codex session. Repeatability and operating outcomes require further evidence.
confidence_and_uncertainty: The stage decision follows the supplied case evidence. Real operating capacity and performance require direct verification.
value_opportunity_implication: Compare buyer effort, review burden and material defects against the manual workflow before extrapolating value.
risk_governance_implication: Retain manual sourcing approval and fallback. Reassess after a material error, loss of authority or a scope change.
recommendation_management_implication: REQUEST EVIDENCE — pilot. P0: procurement director supplies charter delegation and names incident backup. Withhold pilot entry until authority and coverage are evidenced.
change_monitoring_triggers: On a material missed error or loss of stop coverage, pause and revert to manual review.
Reassess before changing the data scope, reviewer capacity or rollout funding.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Who can halt the pilot and who handles incidents during absences? Provide the charter clause or equivalent and the backup roster.
